title: vkit evidence receipt, schema version 2
description: The record of what one check observed, and what that evidence does and does not establish. Written by vkit from an AdapterResult the trusted launcher parsed, never by the candidate. The candidate can supply bytes; the bytes either become a receipt vkit derived or they fail to. `trust_boundary` is required, so a receipt that says nothing about the limits of its own hashes does not validate.

task_id.description: null for a standalone run, which is what makes a run standalone evidence rather than task acceptance.

evidence_kind.description: Derived by evidence_kind(spec) from the check's variant. There is no field a candidate writes that sets this, and a receipt carrying one that disagrees with its check's kind is a contradiction vkit cannot represent.

specification_digest.description: null when the check declares no specification file. Absent is not the same as null, and neither is invented.

digest.description: null means the owner declared no expected digest, not that nothing was measured. vkit's measurement is the value a reader compares.

tool_versions.description: What vkit observed about the tools it launched. An empty object means none were observed, which is a fact rather than a default.

dependencies.description: Over the resolved lock. Empty is honest for a check that declares no dependencies; it is not a claim that there were none.

satisfied.description: The result of each obligation. Every Requirement.obligations member must appear here for the requirement to be discharged; a member with no entry is a gap, not a pass.

assumptions.description: Named, human-readable, and quoted by describe(). An empty list is a claim that there were none, so the field is required rather than omitted.

artifacts.description: Run-relative references. A name that escapes the run directory is refused at parse, not discovered when a report points at it.

sourceIdentity.description: The source inventory the run was measured against, field for field as identity.py records it.

verifierIdentity.description: Which implementation interpreted the output. A receipt whose verifier cannot be named is a receipt about nothing in particular.

limits.description: The execution limits actually in force. A null here is a limit vkit did not impose, recorded as such rather than as a default.

theoremObligation.description: The module is part of the obligation and never inferred from a path an adapter guesses. Two declarations of the same name in two modules are two obligations.

propertyObligation.description: The bounds are part of the obligation rather than a receipt detail, because a run at different bounds is a different claim.

axioms.description: Required and possibly empty. A satisfied theorem with no axiom audit is not a theorem result, so the field has no default.

counterexample.description: A counterexample is variant-agnostic on purpose. Its trace is a string for a TLA+ state sequence, a pytest assertion diff and a Lean error message alike; the thing that has to be typed is the obligation it belongs to.

establishes.description: Copied from ClaimCategory.establishes, so there is one source of these sentences in the repository rather than one per adapter.

does_not_establish.description: Copied from ClaimCategory.does_not_establish. A receipt that states only what it establishes reads as a stronger claim than the evidence supports.

oracle_review.description: The reviewed test or checker source this receipt's evidence rests on. A claim about a human process, which is exactly why it is required and never inferred.

hash_limit.description: What the digests in this receipt do not cover. A digest proves the bytes were these bytes, not that the oracle reading them is right.

normalization.description: The text-level normalization rule cross-platform digests were computed under. A jar is hashed over exact bytes instead, and says so here rather than leaving the reader to guess.
